title: Abinadi Teaches of the Father and the Son
summary: Abinadi addresses an unidentified audience and teaches that God shall come among the children of men and redeem his people. He explains the Father and the Son and says they are one God.

explicit_facts.text: Abinadi speaks to people identified only as “them” and says God shall come among the children of men and redeem his people.
He says that because God dwells in flesh, he shall be called the Son of God, and that the flesh is subjected to the will of the Father.
He explains the terms Father and Son in relation to the power of God and the flesh.
He says they are one God, the Eternal Father of heaven and earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi may be shown speaking to unidentified listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, listeners’ identities, arrangement, clothing, and physical appearances are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: I would that ye should understand that God himself shall come down among the children of men, and shall redeem his people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: And they are one God, yea, the very Eternal Father of heaven and of earth.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: God’s coming and redemption are taught as future events, not narrated as occurring in this scene.
The Father and Son language is a teaching, not a description of visible figures.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the listeners as King Noah’s priests.
Do not depict God or the Son appearing, or show the promised redemption occurring.

title: The Son's Suffering Foretold
summary: The Son does not yield to temptation and suffers mockery, scourging, rejection, and disownment by his people. After working many mighty miracles, he shall be led, crucified, and slain.

explicit_facts.text: The Son suffers temptation but does not yield to it.
He suffers mockery, scourging, being cast out, and being disowned by his people.
After working many mighty miracles among the children of men, he shall be led.
He shall be crucified and slain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi may be shown speaking; the Son's suffering and death are the subject of his teaching, not events occurring in his setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Abinadi's appearance, his audience, and the setting are not specified in these verses.
The Son's appearance and the details of the foretold events are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: And thus the flesh becoming subject to the Spirit, or the Son to the Father, being one God, suffereth temptation, and yieldeth not to the temptation, but suffereth himself to be mocked, and scourged, and cast out, and disowned by his people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: Yea, even so he shall be led, crucified, and slain
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The opening quotation identifies the Son as the subject of the teaching; the later reference to “he” continues that teaching.
The sheep comparison in Mosiah 15:6 is a figure of speech, not a narrated animal scene.
The Son's will is described as being swallowed up in the will of the Father.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the foretold suffering, miracles, or crucifixion as occurring in Abinadi's speaking setting.
Do not depict the sheep comparison as a literal event.
Do not invent an audience, location, appearance, or additional dialogue.

title: Intercession and Redemption
summary: God has gained victory over death and given the Son power to intercede for the children of men. The Son has ascended into heaven, is filled with compassion for them, and has redeemed them.

explicit_facts.text: God breaks the bands of death, gains victory over death, and gives the Son power to intercede for the children of men.
The Son has ascended into heaven, is filled with compassion toward the children of men, stands between them and justice, and has redeemed them.

unspecified_visual_details: No physical appearances or visible setting are specified.

narration.text: And thus God breaketh the bands of death, having gained the victory over death; giving the Son power to make intercession for the children of men—
Having ascended into heaven, having the bowels of mercy; being filled with compassion towards the children of men; standing betwixt them and justice;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses teach intercession and redemption; they do not describe a visible heavenly appearance. Verse 9 does not use the title “the Lord.”
prohibited_inventions: Do not add “the Lord” to a quotation or identify an otherwise unnamed speaker or audience.
Do not depict justice as a person or invent a visible heavenly scene.

title: Who Shall Be His Seed?
summary: Abinadi asks who shall be his seed. He says that those who hearkened to the prophets, believed the Lord would redeem his people, and looked forward to remission of their sins are his seed and heirs of the kingdom of God. He says their sins have been borne and that he died to redeem them.

explicit_facts.text: Abinadi asks who shall be his seed.
Those who hearkened to the prophets, believed the Lord would redeem his people, and looked forward to remission of their sins are called his seed and heirs of the kingdom of God.
Abinadi says their sins have been borne and that he died to redeem them from their transgressions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi addresses listeners, indicated by “you” and “ye.”
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of those called his seed.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now what say ye? And who shall be his seed?

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: For these are they whose sins he has borne; these are they for whom he has died, to redeem them from their transgressions.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage defines his seed through response to the prophets’ words; it does not narrate those people gathering in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent identities for the listeners.
Do not depict a separate offering, death, or gathering as happening during this speech.

title: The Prophets Are His Seed
summary: Abinadi calls the holy prophets “his seed,” describes their proclamations of peace, good tidings, and salvation, and praises their feet upon the mountains.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker calls the holy prophets who have prophesied without falling into transgression “his seed.”
The speaker says these prophets have published peace and salvation, brought good tidings, and said to Zion that God reigns.
The speaker praises their feet upon the mountains.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi is speaking to an audience, though the audience is not identified in these verses.

spoken_dialogue.text: I say unto you that they are his seed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: And these are they who have published peace, who have brought good tidings of good, who have published salvation; and said unto Zion: Thy God reigneth!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: And O how beautiful upon the mountains were their feet!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prophets are described in Abinadi’s teaching, not narrated as physically present.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify or depict a specific audience from these verses.

Do not invent an appearance for the prophets or the referent of “his.”

title: Those Who Publish Peace
summary: The speaker praises those who publish peace now and hereafter, then identifies the Lord as the bringer of good tidings and founder of peace.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker calls the feet of those still publishing peace beautiful upon the mountains.
The speaker praises those who shall hereafter publish peace.
The speaker identifies the Lord as the bringer of good tidings and founder of peace, who has redeemed his people and granted them salvation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker addresses listeners, indicated by “I say unto you.”

title: Redemption and Resurrection
summary: Abinadi speaks of redemption, the Son’s power over the dead, and a first resurrection.

explicit_facts.text: Redemption was prepared from the foundation of the world; without it, all mankind must have perished.
The bands of death shall be broken; the Son reigns, has power over the dead, and brings about the resurrection of the dead.
A first resurrection includes those who have been, who are, and who shall be, until the resurrection of Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi is addressing listeners, as indicated by “I say unto you.”

spoken_dialogue.text: I say unto you, were it not for this, all mankind must have perished.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, the bands of death shall be broken, and the Son reigneth, and hath power over the dead; therefore, he bringeth to pass the resurrection of the dead.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: And there cometh a resurrection, even a first resurrection;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses teach about redemption and resurrection; they do not narrate a visible resurrection occurring during the speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Son appearing or dead people rising during this speech.
Do not depict the bands of death as literal visible restraints.

title: The First Resurrection
summary: The verses teach that prophets, those who believed their words, and those who kept God's commandments shall come forth in the first resurrection. They also say that those who died before Christ came without having salvation declared to them have part in it.

explicit_facts.text: The prophets, those who believed their words, and those who kept God's commandments shall come forth in the first resurrection.
They are raised to dwell with God and have eternal life through Christ.
Those who died before Christ came in ignorance, without having salvation declared to them, have part in the first resurrection and are redeemed by the Lord.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearances of those described are not specified.

and these are they that have died before Christ came, in their ignorance, not having salvation declared unto them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The resurrection and restoration are taught here, not narrated as visible events occurring in a specified setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a speaker or audience from these verses alone.
Do not depict the resurrection or restoration as a present-tense visible event.
Do not invent appearances for God, Christ, the Lord, or those described.

title: A Warning About Rebellion
summary: Abinadi teaches that little children have eternal life. He warns that those who knowingly rebel against God and die in their sins have no part in the first resurrection, and says the Lord cannot deny justice.

explicit_facts.text: Little children have eternal life.
Those who knowingly rebel against God, do not keep his commandments, and die in their sins have no part in the first resurrection.
Salvation does not come to such people; the Lord cannot deny justice when it has its claim.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi is speaking to listeners addressed as “ye.”

title: Abinadi Speaks of Salvation
summary: Abinadi says the Lord’s salvation will be declared to every people. His prophetic words speak of watchmen singing, Jerusalem’s redemption, and the ends of the earth seeing salvation.

explicit_facts.text: Abinadi says the Lord’s salvation will be declared to every nation, kindred, tongue, and people.
The prophetic words say watchmen will lift their voices and sing when the Lord brings again Zion.
The words call on Jerusalem’s waste places to sing and say the Lord has comforted his people and redeemed Jerusalem.
The words say the Lord has made bare his holy arm before the nations and that all the ends of the earth shall see God’s salvation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi speaks; the watchmen and Jerusalem are subjects of his prophetic words, not figures shown alongside him.
unspecified_visual_details: Abinadi’s appearance, audience, and surroundings are not specified in these verses.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Abinadi

spoken_dialogue.text: Break forth into joy, sing together, ye waste places of Jerusalem;

spoken_dialogue.text: and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verses 29–31 shift into prophetic words addressing the Lord and Jerusalem. Abinadi voices these words; the verses do not identify the watchmen as their present speakers.

Do not stage the foretold events as occurring during Abinadi’s speech.
